confirmed: Source version, title, and authors match the journal document: Shen, Lee, and He, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1956939, published 02 October 2026, received 03 August 2026 and accepted 16 September 2026; PDF has 27 pages (p. 1 and PDF page count).

The complete on-file markdown, including the reference list, was read. Supplementary Material S1 is an external Questionnaire Instrument, not an appendix included in this PDF (p. 7, Section 3.1.3; p. 25, Supplementary material).

One course-based observational study, with no randomized AI-assistance experiment: quasi_people and observational context are appropriate; this is not a synthesis (p. 5, Section 3.1.1; p. 24, Section 7).

The four intact classes contained 151 students; 136 nonduplicated questionnaires remained after one duplicate was removed, and three incomplete responses were excluded, leaving 133 analyzed people. n_randomized = null is appropriate; the analyzed sample is not below 50 (p. 5, Section 3.1.1).

The analyzed sample contains 38 first-year, 34 second-year, and 61 third-year students in Character Design and Animation Concept Design at Communication University of Zhejiang, China (p. 5, Section 3.1.1; p. 1, affiliation).

The main questionnaire definition identifies 74 AI users. AI-help percentage has mean 19.632 and SD 20.539; AI-content percentage has mean 12.158 and SD 17.412. These are perceived involvement, not logged usage (p. 12, Table 3; p. 7, Section 3.1.3).

Two instructors initially scored the artworks without questionnaire or AI-use information; five 20-point dimensions sum to a maximum of 100. Kappa = 0.92 before reconciliation; a third evaluator was used for discrepancies exceeding 5% (pp. 5–6, Section 3.1.2).
All four recorded outcomes have N = 133 in the descriptive table; the scores are reconciled student-level results rather than separate rater observations (p. 10, Table 1; p. 6, Section 3.1.2).
S1-O1 Figure 4 values match: AI use −0.01, assistive use 0.04, content-generative use −0.01, baseline 0.39***. S1-O4 values match: −0.01, 0.14, −0.14, baseline 0.42*** (p. 13, Figure 4).

S1-O2 Figure 4 values match: AI use −0.01, assistive use 0.08, content-generative use −0.13. S1-O3 values match: −0.08, −0.12, −0.20. None of these AI coefficients has a significance marker (p. 13, Figure 4).
Final total: PSM ATT −1.581, 95% CI [−4.297, 0.946]; IPW ATE −1.094, 95% CI [−4.028, 2.063]. These match the reported string and one-line finding (p. 14, Table 4).
Authorship: PSM ATT −1.270, 95% CI [−1.892, −0.743]; IPW ATE −1.008, 95% CI [−1.648, −0.341]. These match the reported string and one-line finding (p. 14, Table 4).

Table 4 reports Treated N = 74 and Matched N = 30. The latter counts unique matched controls under matching with replacement, not total analyzed people or randomized participants (p. 14, Table 4 and note).
Below-maximum authorship logit for AI use: coefficient 1.542, OR 4.672, SE 0.408, FDR p < 0.001; all correctly transcribed (p. 14, Table 5).
Authorship by AI-content group: 0%, N = 66, mean 19.38; 1%–20%, N = 40, mean 19.00; >20%, N = 27, mean 17.30; ANOVA F = 10.34, p < 0.001. All correctly transcribed (p. 19, Table 8 and note).

The article reports no outcome measuring diversity or similarity across students' creative outputs; its other outcome families are questionnaire measures (pp. 5–9, Sections 3.1–3.2; pp. 12–22, Sections 4.2–4.4).

No named AI model, public dataset URL, or code URL is provided. The data availability statement describes confidential data available only by request and agreement (pp. 6–7, Section 3.1.3; p. 25, Data availability statement).
summary: This is observational evidence from 133 students, with no randomized AI-assistance study, and all transcribed numerical results match the PDF. Six corrections address construct coding, omitted outcomes and change-score results, incomplete eligibility and statistics fields, and overly strong wording of null findings.
